lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The same 2,300-merchant onboarding result is attributed to both Harbor Payments and the hospital practicum, with different reductions.
items.because: A reader may doubt which entry owns the achievement and which figures are accurate.

items.says: The résumé includes a date of birth and nationality, personal details conventionally left off.
items.because: They are not relevant to assessing qualifications and use space without helping the application.

items.says: Education appears before Experience, so the page does not open with the work history and product internship.
items.because: The work history and product internship make a stronger opening for the résumé’s product direction.

items.says: The line attributes the 35% increase to the flow change and extends it to all merchants without evidence for either claim.
items.because: Other changes could explain a before-and-after increase, and results for some merchants would not establish a result for all.

items.says: The 35% figure has no comparison point and does not say whether it is relative or a percentage-point change.
items.because: Without that anchor, a reader cannot tell how conversion was measured or judge the improvement’s size.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not establish that the redesign caused any difference.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who stayed on the old flow in ways that affect onboarding outcomes.

items.says: The bullet gives a comparison method but no measured result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what outcome was measured or whether the comparison showed an improvement.

items.says: The key result is buried after the method and scale.
items.because: A scanning reader may pass over the reduction in time to first payment.

items.says: The line reports a reduction in late deliveries by changing which shipments count, making the rates incomparable.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments can lower the reported rate without reducing late deliveries.

items.says: The S&OP bullet names the process and forecast pack but gives no outcome.
items.because: It does not show what the reviews or pack changed about planning or decisions.

items.says: “Prepares” is present tense even though the role ended in August 2023.
items.because: The tense shift breaks consistency in a description of a completed role.

items.says: The main result appears after the rollout and training details.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the annual driver-hours saving.

items.says: The weekly-active-user result comes after the interview context.
items.because: That growth is the clearest evidence of impact, but a reader scanning the opening may not reach it.

items.says: The weekly sessions are described without stating what changed as a result.
items.because: A reader cannot tell whether they led to a decision or improvement.

items.says: The intake-form change has no measure of its scale or effect.
items.because: Staff adoption does not show how substantial the change was or what it did to intake.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding result is attributed to the hospital practicum even though it repeats the Harbor Payments internship result.
items.because: The other practicum bullets concern clinics, so this assigns a separate role’s result to the hospital project.

items.says: The merchant-onboarding claim shifts the entry away from its hospital-project focus.
items.because: Merchant onboarding is unrelated to the scheduling and intake work and repeats the internship story.
